beats.say: A penny gets you a library. And the library costs you later.
Sign up for 12 records for a penny, no catalog listed.
Or choose the regular plan, pay per album at club price.
Or pick the premium bundle, extra titles for a higher fee.
Members must buy a minimum number of albums at full price. Sounds generous.
But it does a job: the penny locks you into automatic shipments.
If you don't say no by the deadline, the next record ships with a full-price bill.
That clause turned a one-cent hook into a $1.4 billion peak in 1996.
When sales fell, the same clause left only $17 million by 2014, leading to bankruptcy in 2015.
Gym: free trial week, then a $30 class pack you must buy.
Café: free pastry, then a $15 coffee bundle you're expected to take.
Streaming app: free month, then a $12 premium plan feels like the logical next step.
Watch for hidden minimum commitments. Follow for more.
